label: B2B software, clean pause test
note: 28 days on and 28 days off with no promotions. About 34% of paid brand clicks are truly extra, so the program earns its money.

label: HVAC, messy export
note: US dates, quoted thousands, "n/a" cells, duplicate days and a footer row. Choose the click columns by hand, because the automatic pick is wrong; the right answer is about 68% incremental.

label: Pause during a sitewide sale
note: Brand ads were switched off the same day a sale began, so organic clicks tripled. The test cannot separate the two effects, so treat it as inconclusive.

label: Bids cut instead of paused
note: Ads were reduced by about 80% instead of switched off. Divide by the clicks actually lost, which gives roughly 9% incremental, not the 27% the pre-pause number suggests.

label: Pause during rising giving-season demand
note: Demand was climbing every day anyway, so the rise in organic clicks is not all recapture. A pause timed on a ramp is not decision grade.
